newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures end soft following LME.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures end soft following LME.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures closed slightly lower on Friday, with news of higher Japanese premiums for the third quarter limiting falls triggered by a lower close in London overnight, traders said.

"For the falls we've seen in London overnight, aluminium futures here didn't drop much," said one trader. "The news on third-quarter premiums lent some support, though future direction remains uncertain."
TOCOM benchmark April 1998 shed 0.8 yen to finish at 196.0 yen per kg, which compared with 193.3 yen at the end of last week. Other contracts lost between 0.5 and 2.1 yen.
Estimated volume was 2,337 lots, up from 1,902 on Thursday.
Traders said Japanese aluminium supply contract premiums climbed to $86-89 a tonne for the July-September quarter, up some $5 from second-quarter deliveries.
In London overnight, three-month aluminium slid $23 to $1,622 per tonne, despite a 3,700 tonne stocks drawdown.
